reform_name: State multifamily zoning floor in urbanized areas
description: Mandate by-right multifamily on all parcels >=4,000 sqft within 0.5 mi of frequent transit, employment centers, and commercial corridors; floor binds notwithstanding charter-city home rule.
notes: Statewide-concern doctrine sustains; SB 9/SB 35/SB 423 precedent. Charter cities have lost similar challenges (CHF v. Berkeley, Bldg Industry v. SF).

reform_name: Missing-middle by-right (4-12 unit buildings on residential parcels)
description: Allow fourplexes, sixplexes, cottage courts, townhomes, and small apartment buildings on parcels currently zoned R-1 or R-2 in urbanized areas, subject to objective standards.
notes: SB 9 narrow precedent. Auckland and Minneapolis comparators show modest but real production gains over 5-10 yrs.

description: Statewide ministerial approval for adaptive reuse of obsolete office, retail, hotel, and parking sites to residential, with objective standards on egress/seismic/fire only.
notes: AB 2011/AB 1633 trajectory. Cost economics depend on building geometry; not a silver bullet. Evidence: medium.

description: Allow housing on land owned by religious institutions, hospitals, universities, and nonprofits by right under objective standards (SB 4 expansion).
notes: SB 4 (Wiener) precedent already in force. Medium impact ceiling but politically tractable.

description: All surplus public land in urbanized areas presumptively available for housing, with state Office of Land Use empowered to override local objections to specific parcels.
notes: Surplus Land Act extension. School-district land is politically thorny (Prop 39 history).

reform_name: SB 79 transit-oriented density as floor not ceiling
description: Treat SB 79 TOD densities as floors that local governments cannot reduce; pre-empt local downzonings and overlay restrictions within station areas.
notes: SB 79 already enacted. The floor-not-ceiling framing is the binding question.

reform_name: Ministerial approval with strict shot clocks and deemed-approved
description: 60-day shot clock for ministerial review of qualifying projects; missed deadline = automatic approval. State backstop for repeated violations.
notes: Permit Streamlining Act extension. SB 35/423 model. Strong evidence base.

reform_name: Objective standards mandate for all residential review
description: Bar discretionary design review, subjective neighborhood compatibility findings, and aesthetic veto for residential projects meeting objective standards.
notes: Housing Accountability Act expansion. Empirical base: strong.

description: New state Office of Housing Approval with authority to issue binding approvals when local agencies miss deadlines, apply invalid standards, or repeatedly violate state law; escalating fines and deemed approvals.
notes: Critical to making preemption real. Will be litigated; Sole-state-concern doctrine should hold.

reform_name: CEQA exemption for infill housing and adaptive reuse
description: Statutory CEQA exemption for infill housing, mixed-use infill, and adaptive reuse meeting objective standards; preserves federal NEPA, Coastal Act, tribal consultation, and seismic/hazmat rules.
notes: AB 130/SB 131 baseline trajectory. Single most impactful CEQA reform per project.

description: Categorical CEQA exemption for grid upgrades, transformer/substation installs, water/sewer rehab, bus-priority lanes, active transportation, and energy storage.
notes: Necessary corollary to housing reforms. Bus-priority CEQA reform already partially enacted (SB 922).

reform_name: Anti-CEQA-abuse: mandatory loser-pays in non-environmental CEQA suits
description: Where CEQA litigation is brought primarily for non-environmental purposes (NIMBY blocking, labor leverage), losing plaintiff pays defendant fees.
notes: Politically toxic. Excluded from central scenario; useful only if courts uphold a narrower abuse standard.

reform_name: Standardized statewide impact-fee schedule with nexus caps
description: Cap impact fees at percent of project value or at evidentiary nexus, whichever is lower; require transparent fee schedules; no late-stage surprise fees.
notes: AB 602 baseline. Real but second-order impact.

description: Cap inclusionary requirements at level shown by feasibility study to not block production; if local inclusionary kills feasibility, state defaults to lower percentage.
notes: Affordable-housing politics. Useful but excluded from central to keep coalition.

description: Expand Enhanced Infrastructure Financing Districts and similar tools; state matches local infrastructure bonds in growth corridors; LA-share property tax increment can fund growth-enabling infrastructure.
notes: Post-redevelopment fiscal plumbing fix. Without it, growth dividend leaks.

description: Allow single-stair multifamily up to 6 stories with sprinklers and modern egress, harmonized statewide.
notes: Seattle, Honolulu, Vancouver have done it. Modest cost reduction; widens feasibility envelope on small lots.

reform_name: Modular and factory-built housing fast-track approvals
description: Statewide approval body for modular/factory-built housing types; pre-approved plans valid in any jurisdiction.
notes: HCD already does some of this. Bigger upside if combined with construction-defect liability reform.

description: Pre-approved multifamily building designs (3-, 4-, 6-plex, courtyard apartments) with standardized engineering; locals must accept by-right.
notes: Reduces architecture/engineering cost on small projects substantially.

description: Cap statute of limitations and tort exposure on multifamily condo construction defects to make condo construction insurable again.
notes: Plaintiffs bar opposition is intense. Without this, condo construction stays near zero.

reform_name: Parking minimum elimination near transit and corridors
description: AB 2097 expansion: zero parking minimums on parcels within 0.5 mi of transit OR commercial corridors OR jobs centers; no de facto parking requirements via traffic study.
notes: AB 2097 already does much of this. High leverage per unit cost.

description: 60-day plan review and 120-day energization SLA for new multifamily; missed deadline = deemed-energized for occupancy purposes; CPUC enforcement; transparent capacity maps.
notes: LADWP is municipal; legal mechanism differs (state utility regulation + LA charter). Most leveraged single utility reform.

description: State acts as group buyer/standardization body for distribution transformers; bulk-purchase contracts and stockpile reduce 18+ month lead times.
notes: Federal IRA funding leverage. Direct binding constraint.

description: Mandate joint trenching for water/sewer/electric/fiber in any street project; reduces serial outages and per-unit infrastructure cost.
notes: Cost savings reinvest into capacity.

description: Standardized electrical-service designs for common multifamily building types accepted by all utilities without bespoke plan review.
notes: Quick win.

description: Restaurants, cafes, bars, gyms, clinics, childcare, and small venues by-right in commercial and mixed-use zones, subject to objective health/fire/noise standards. CUP abuse limited.
notes: Empirically weaker evidence base than housing reform — flag as medium-confidence.

description: COVID-era outdoor dining permits made permanent statewide; small entertainment venues operable under objective noise/safety/operating-hours standards.
notes: Politically popular. Real but modest impact.

description: Single statewide form and timeline for tenant-improvement health/fire/building signoffs; eliminates duplicative city-county approval chains.
notes: Legal collision risk: county health departments will resist.

description: Limit conditional use permits as a discretionary commercial veto where state economic development policy is impaired; preempt formula-retail bans that conflict with statewide policy.
notes: Charter-city / 1st amendment / local merchant politics. Excluded from central scenario.

reform_name: State permitting surge teams and building-dept staffing grants
description: State pays for additional plan checkers, inspectors, and permit staff in jurisdictions with permit-velocity below threshold; surge teams deployable for backlog reduction.
notes: Cheap, fast, popular. Underrated reform.

description: Apprenticeship pipeline expansion for electricians, plumbers, elevator techs, inspectors, and utility crews; coordinated with community colleges and unions.
notes: Long lead time; labor capacity caps everything.

description: Permanent design-build authority for housing-enabling infrastructure (utilities, transit, streets); standardized P3 templates.
notes: Procurement reform yields material time savings.

reform_name: Anti-sabotage compliance audit and penalty regime
description: HCD authorized to audit local approval records; jurisdictions with documented sabotage face escalating fines and Builder's Remedy expansion.
notes: Necessary teeth; without it, cities comply on paper and obstruct in practice.

reform_name: Coastal Act delegation reform for non-shoreline parcels
description: Clarify Coastal Act jurisdiction so parcels beyond direct shoreline impact are not subject to Coastal Commission appeal; preserve genuine coastal protection.
notes: Coastal Commission constitutionally protected; reform is hard. Excluded from central.

description: State reinsurance pool for builder's risk and condo construction insurance to reduce capital-market risk on new construction.
notes: Promising but new mechanism. Watch as separate track.

description: Within Prop 13 1% cap, modify ERAF and post-1992 allocation rules so growth-impacted jurisdictions receive a larger share of new construction property tax — reduces fiscal misalignment.
notes: Schools coalition opposition. Excluded from central; included only if politics shift.
